## Interview Summary

On September 12, 2023, the reviewing analyst conducted a telephone interview with the relationship manager assigned to the Oakhurst Logistics Partners LP account. The interview sought to establish the circumstances surrounding the initiation of the $2,715,243.14 outbound wire transfer on September 8, 2023. The relationship manager confirmed that the wire request was received via email from an address purporting to belong to the customer's Chief Financial Officer. The reviewing analyst asked if the relationship manager had verified the email address against the customer's profile. The relationship manager stated that the email address appeared correct at first glance, noting that the sender name matched the customer's Chief Financial Officer. The reviewing analyst pointed out that the domain in the sender's email address differed by one character from the domain registered for Oakhurst Logistics Partners LP in the bank's system. The relationship manager acknowledged this discrepancy, stating they had not noticed the minor variation during the processing of the request.

The reviewing analyst then inquired about the bank's standard procedures for verifying high-value wire transfers, specifically regarding the dual-approval control. The relationship manager explained that bank policy requires telephone confirmation with an authorized signatory for any wire transfer exceeding a low six-figure sum when initiated via email. The reviewing analyst noted that the transaction record did not indicate a telephone confirmation had occurred for the $2,715,243.14 transfer. The relationship manager stated that the email requesting the wire transfer contained language emphasizing extreme urgency, claiming the funds were required immediately to secure a critical shipment of materials from Slateford Imports Enterprises LLC. The relationship manager explained that due to the stated urgency and the proximity to the daily wire cutoff time, they bypassed the telephone confirmation requirement to ensure the transfer was processed on September 8, 2023.

The reviewing analyst asked about the beneficiary information provided in the wire request. The relationship manager stated the instructions directed funds to Bastion Distribution Holdings Ltd. The reviewing analyst noted that Oakhurst Logistics Partners LP's transaction history showed no previous transfers to this entity and that the customer's business profile indicated its primary suppliers were Redstone Metals Enterprises LLC and Cornerstone Fabrication LLC. The relationship manager confirmed they had not previously processed transfers to Bastion Distribution Holdings Ltd. for this customer. When asked if they found the new beneficiary unusual, the relationship manager stated they assumed Bastion Distribution Holdings Ltd. was a new supplier or a subsidiary of an existing supplier, given the context of the urgent materials shipment mentioned in the email. The reviewing analyst pointed out that the email referenced a shipment from Slateford Imports Enterprises LLC, but the beneficiary name on the wire instructions was Bastion Distribution Holdings Ltd. The relationship manager stated they had not noticed this discrepancy at the time.

Following the interview with the relationship manager, the reviewing analyst spoke with the branch operations manager who authorized the release of the wire transfer on September 8, 2023. The branch operations manager confirmed they reviewed the wire request submitted by the relationship manager. The reviewing analyst asked about the branch operations manager's review process, specifically regarding the bypassed dual-approval control. The branch operations manager stated they noted the absence of telephone confirmation but approved the release based on the relationship manager's notation that the transfer was extremely urgent and the email originated from the customer's Chief Financial Officer. The branch operations manager explained they relied on the relationship manager's assessment of the situation, given the relationship manager's familiarity with the customer.

The reviewing analyst asked the branch operations manager if they had reviewed the beneficiary information or the sender's email address. The branch operations manager stated they primarily focused on ensuring the account had sufficient funds to cover the $2,715,243.14 transfer and that the request was processed before the wire cutoff. They confirmed they had not independently verified the email address domain or the beneficiary name against the customer's historical activity or known suppliers. The branch operations manager acknowledged that the transfer was initiated minutes before the wire cutoff, which contributed to the expedited review process.

On September 14, 2023, after the bank received notification from Oakhurst Logistics Partners LP that the wire transfer was fraudulent, the reviewing analyst, accompanied by the relationship manager, conducted an in-person interview with the customer's Chief Financial Officer. The Chief Financial Officer confirmed they had not initiated or authorized the $2,715,243.14 wire transfer to Bastion Distribution Holdings Ltd. on September 8, 2023. The reviewing analyst presented a copy of the email request received by the relationship manager. The Chief Financial Officer stated the email address was a lookalike domain and did not belong to Oakhurst Logistics Partners LP.

The Chief Financial Officer reviewed the wire instructions and confirmed that Bastion Distribution Holdings Ltd. was not a known vendor or supplier for Oakhurst Logistics Partners LP. They further stated that the company had no pending transactions or business relationship with Slateford Imports Enterprises LLC, the entity mentioned in the fraudulent email as the supplier requiring urgent payment. The reviewing analyst asked if the Chief Financial Officer could provide any insight into how the fraudulent actors might have obtained information about the company's internal procedures or personnel. The Chief Financial Officer stated they were conducting an internal investigation to determine if their systems had been compromised but could not provide definitive answers at that time.

The reviewing analyst discussed the recovery efforts with the Chief Financial Officer, noting that Cortex Bank and Trust had contacted the receiving institution upon discovery of the fraud. The reviewing analyst informed the customer that the receiving institution had successfully frozen a portion of the funds. The reviewing analyst explained that $597,353.49 of the original wire amount had been secured, leaving a residual loss to the customer of $2,117,889.65. The Chief Financial Officer acknowledged this information and stated they would be working with law enforcement regarding the remaining unrecovered funds. The customer confirmed they had implemented enhanced security measures, including mandatory verbal confirmation for all wire transfers, regardless of urgency or origin, to prevent similar incidents in the future. The customer also stated they had communicated the updated procedures to all authorized signatories and relevant bank personnel, including the relationship manager. The interview concluded with the reviewing analyst advising the customer that Cortex Bank and Trust would continue to cooperate with the receiving institution and law enforcement regarding the frozen funds.

## Key Finding

The review established that the compromised vendor communication originated from a lookalike sender domain differing by one character from the vendor's established contact address. The funds transfer was initiated minutes before the wire cutoff time on August 30, 2023. The beneficiary name on the transfer instructions did not match the invoicing vendor. Analysis of the counterparty information revealed that $2,263,757.50 of the induced funds was subsequently traced to an account held by Oakhurst Management Group LLC at an external institution. The reviewing analyst confirmed this attribution on June 24, 2024, identifying the receiving account as 89-84110-9.

## Applicable Policy and Regulatory Reference

The activity identified in the account held by Valentina Grimaldi requires review against Cortex Bank and Trust policies governing the detection and reporting of suspected wire fraud. The activity is evaluated in the context of the Bank Secrecy Act and its implementing regulations, which mandate the filing of a Suspicious Activity Report when a financial institution detects a known or suspected violation of federal law, a suspicious transaction related to a money laundering activity, or a violation of the Bank Secrecy Act. The regulatory framework establishes specific reporting thresholds based on the circumstances of the identified activity. The threshold for mandatory reporting is established at the $5,000 suspicious activity reporting mark when a suspect can be identified. In instances where no suspect can be identified, the threshold is elevated to the $25,000 level. The activity under review in the Valentina Grimaldi account, which involves a fraudulent outbound wire transfer, exceeds these thresholds, necessitating evaluation for potential reporting obligations.

The internal procedures at Cortex Bank and Trust designed to identify and mitigate the risks associated with fraudulent wire transfers are central to this review. ## Internal Escalation and Committee Deliberation

Following the initial investigation by the Financial Intelligence Unit, the reviewing analyst recommended the matter for escalation. This recommendation was based on the identification of a significant fraudulent outbound wire transfer and the subsequent identification of several red flags indicative of wire fraud, including the use of a lookalike sender domain and a beneficiary name that did not match the invoicing vendor. The reviewing analyst also noted the substantial residual loss to the customer, which amounted to $2,117,889.65 after $597,353.49 was successfully frozen at the receiving institution. The initial review of the activity associated with Lorcan Hawthorne, Cortex Bank and Trust account 84-86518-1, concluded on September 18, 2023. The reviewing analyst documented these findings in an internal referral, which was then submitted to the Financial Intelligence Unit management team for review.

On September 20, 2023, the Financial Intelligence Unit management team reviewed the analyst’s findings. The management review concurred with the initial assessment that the activity was consistent with wire fraud. The management team noted that the fraudulent outbound wire amount of $2,715,243.14 was a substantial transaction and that the circumstances surrounding the transfer warranted further scrutiny. The management team specifically highlighted the observation that the funds transfer was initiated minutes before the wire cutoff time, a tactic sometimes employed to circumvent standard review processes. Furthermore, the management team considered the red flag concerning the urgency language used to override the dual-approval control, which was a critical factor in the successful execution of the fraudulent transfer. Based on these considerations, the Financial Intelligence Unit management team determined that the case met the criteria for escalation to the Suspicious Activity Review Committee.

The Suspicious Activity Review Committee convened to discuss the escalated case concerning Lorcan Hawthorne. The committee members reviewed the investigation report and the supporting documentation provided by the Financial Intelligence Unit. The committee's deliberation focused on the nature of the fraudulent activity and the potential implications for Cortex Bank and Trust. The committee considered the specific red flags identified during the investigation. The use of a lookalike sender domain, differing by only one character from a legitimate domain, was recognized as a sophisticated deception tactic designed to mislead the customer. The committee also discussed the discrepancy between the beneficiary name and the invoicing vendor, which is a common indicator of business email compromise and related wire fraud typologies.

During the committee's deliberation, there was discussion regarding the extent of the bank's liability and the effectiveness of the existing internal controls. One committee member raised a question regarding the circumstances under which the dual-approval control was overridden. The committee reviewed the communication associated with the wire transfer request, noting the urgency language that was used to justify bypassing the established control. The discussion acknowledged that while the customer initiated the transfer, the deception involved in inducing the payment was a critical element of the fraud. The committee recognized that the transaction involved funds induced out of a customer account by deception and moved by wire to a beneficiary the customer never intended to pay.

The committee also reviewed the recovery efforts and the financial impact of the incident. The committee noted that while a portion of the funds, $597,353.49, was successfully frozen at the receiving institution, the residual loss to the customer remained significant at $2,117,889.65. The committee considered whether the significant financial loss and the sophisticated nature of the fraud necessitated a broader review of similar accounts or transactions, although this case review was specifically focused on the activity associated with Lorcan Hawthorne.

There was no formal dissent recorded during the Suspicious Activity Review Committee's deliberation regarding the nature of the activity. The committee members were in agreement that the activity observed was highly suspicious and consistent with wire fraud. However, there was some discussion regarding the specific narrative details to be included in the regulatory filing to ensure that the sophisticated nature of the deception, particularly the use of the lookalike domain and the urgency language, was clearly articulated. The committee emphasized the importance of accurately describing the red flags to provide law enforcement with actionable intelligence.

Following the thorough deliberation, the Suspicious Activity Review Committee reached a consensus decision. The committee determined that the activity associated with Lorcan Hawthorne, Cortex Bank and Trust account 84-86518-1, met the regulatory requirements for filing a Suspicious Activity Report. The decision was based on the aggregate findings of the investigation, including the substantial fraudulent outbound wire amount, the specific red flags indicative of deception, and the resulting financial loss. The committee directed the Financial Intelligence Unit to proceed with drafting the Suspicious Activity Report narrative, ensuring that all relevant details discussed during the deliberation were accurately incorporated. The committee also recommended that the relationship manager for Lorcan Hawthorne be briefed on the situation, in accordance with the bank's internal communication protocols regarding suspected fraudulent activity, to facilitate any necessary customer support and to review the customer's security practices. The committee's decision to file was documented in the internal case management system, concluding the formal escalation and deliberation process for this specific case review.

## Remediation and Account Restriction Actions

Upon determining that Isadora Balogun had induced an unauthorized wire transfer from account 62-78890-2 to Sandpiper Imports Holdings Ltd. in the amount of $2,715,243.14, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated immediate protective measures. The reviewing analyst, in consultation with the FIU manager, applied a hard hold to the subject account. This restriction prevented all outgoing funds transfers, including ACH originations, domestic and international wire transfers, and internal book transfers, effectively freezing the remaining balance. The hold was placed on September 18, 2023, shortly after the fraudulent transaction was identified and the recall request was transmitted to the receiving institution. This action was necessary to mitigate further potential losses and secure the account pending a comprehensive review of the customer's relationship and the surrounding circumstances. Following the application of the hard hold, the relationship manager was notified of the incident and instructed to contact the customer. The customer was informed that a suspicious transaction had been detected and that their account had been temporarily restricted pending investigation. The relationship manager gathered initial information from the customer regarding the circumstances of the wire request, which involved a communication purportedly from a known vendor, Cornerstone Fabrication LLC, directing payment to a new account held by Sandpiper Imports Holdings Ltd.

Subsequent to the placement of the hard hold, Cortex Bank and Trust’s fraud operations unit attempted to recover the funds transferred to Sandpiper Imports Holdings Ltd. A formal recall request was issued to the receiving institution, citing suspected fraud. The receiving institution acknowledged the recall request but indicated that the funds had been partially dissipated. On September 20, 2023, the receiving institution confirmed that a portion of the funds, totaling $597,353.49, had been successfully frozen in the beneficiary account. These funds were subsequently returned to Cortex Bank and Trust and credited back to Isadora Balogun's account. However, the remaining balance of the original transfer, amounting to $2,117,889.65, was unrecoverable. The customer was informed of the partial recovery and the residual loss. The reviewing analyst documented the recovery efforts and the final disposition of the funds in the case management system. The significant residual loss highlighted the severity of the incident and underscored the need for enhanced security measures and ongoing monitoring of the customer's accounts.

In light of the incident and the identified vulnerabilities, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a comprehensive review of Isadora Balogun’s overall relationship. The review encompassed all accounts associated with the customer, including those held jointly or in a fiduciary capacity. The objective was to assess the customer's susceptibility to social engineering and to evaluate the effectiveness of the bank's existing controls. The review identified several areas of concern. The fraudulent wire request was initiated based on an email containing a lookalike sender domain that differed from the legitimate vendor's domain by a single character. Furthermore, the email contained urgency language that pressured the customer to bypass established internal controls, specifically the dual-approval requirement for large outgoing wires. The customer's failure to recognize these red flags and to adhere to established security protocols raised significant concerns regarding their ability to safeguard their accounts against sophisticated fraud schemes. The review also noted that the beneficiary name on the wire request, Sandpiper Imports Holdings Ltd., did not match the name of the invoicing vendor, Cornerstone Fabrication LLC, a discrepancy that should have prompted further scrutiny by the customer.

Based on the findings of the relationship review, Cortex Bank and Trust implemented several remediation measures. The hard hold on account 62-78890-2 was lifted on September 25, 2023, following the completion of the initial investigation and the implementation of enhanced security protocols. However, the account remained subject to channel limitations. Specifically, the customer's ability to initiate wire transfers via the online banking platform was permanently revoked. All future wire requests must be initiated in person at a branch location or via a recorded telephone call with a dedicated relationship manager, subject to enhanced authentication procedures, including out-of-band verification and secondary approval by a senior bank officer. These channel limitations were deemed necessary to mitigate the risk of future unauthorized transfers and to ensure that all outgoing wires are subject to rigorous scrutiny. The customer was informed of these changes and the rationale behind them. Additionally, the customer was provided with educational materials regarding common fraud typologies, including business email compromise and vendor impersonation schemes, and was strongly encouraged to implement robust internal controls to prevent similar incidents in the future.

In addition to the channel limitations, Isadora Balogun's accounts were subjected to enhanced monitoring rules within the bank's transaction monitoring system. These rules were specifically designed to detect patterns of activity consistent with the observed typology. The enhanced monitoring profile includes lower thresholds for alerts generated by outgoing wire transfers and ACH originations, particularly those directed to new or unfamiliar beneficiaries. The system was also configured to flag transactions involving beneficiaries located in high-risk jurisdictions or those associated with known fraud networks. Furthermore, the monitoring rules were adjusted to prioritize alerts generated by transactions that occur outside of normal business hours or those that exhibit unusual characteristics, such as the wire transfer in this case, which was initiated minutes before the daily cutoff time. The enhanced monitoring profile will remain in effect for a minimum of twelve months, subject to periodic review and adjustment based on the customer's ongoing activity and risk profile.

The FIU also conducted a review of the other subjects identified in this case, including Lorcan Hawthorne, Greystone Ventures Corp., Valentina Grimaldi, and Oakhurst Logistics Partners LP, to determine if their accounts exhibited similar vulnerabilities or suspicious activity. While no direct evidence of fraud was identified in connection with these accounts during the review period, their proximity to the primary subject and their involvement in related business activities warranted increased scrutiny. The reviewing analyst recommended that these accounts be subjected to heightened monitoring for a period of six months. This monitoring will focus on detecting unusual patterns of funds transfers, changes in beneficiary profiles, and any activity that deviates from established historical norms. The relationship managers for these accounts were also notified of the incident and instructed to remain vigilant for any signs of potential fraud or social engineering.

The decision to retain Isadora Balogun as a customer was made after careful consideration of the incident, the implemented remediation measures, and the customer's overall relationship history. The bank determined that the risk of future fraud could be adequately managed through the channel limitations, the enhanced monitoring rules, and the ongoing educational efforts. However, the customer's relationship will be subject to ongoing review, and any future incidents or indications of increased risk may result in a reevaluation of this decision, up to and including account closure. The bank remains committed to monitoring the customer's activity and to taking all necessary steps to protect its assets and those of its customers. The FIU will continue to monitor the accounts associated with all subjects identified in this report for a period of ninety days following the filing of this Suspicious Activity Report. This monitoring will be conducted to identify any subsequent suspicious activity, including attempts to circumvent the implemented controls or to initiate unauthorized transactions. The results of this ongoing monitoring will be documented in the case management system and may form the basis for future regulatory filings or further restrictive actions. The bank's commitment to robust BSA/AML compliance and fraud prevention remains a priority, and all identified vulnerabilities will be addressed through ongoing training, system enhancements, and the rigorous application of established policies and procedures.

## Law Enforcement Coordination and Information Sharing

On September 11, 2023, Cortex Bank and Trust received a federal grand jury subpoena from the United States Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York. The subpoena requested all account opening documents, signature cards, monthly statements, wire transfer records, and correspondence relating to the account held by Greystone Ventures Corp., account number 50-45430-3. The request specified a date range encompassing the entirety of the review period. The reviewing analyst compiled the requested documentation, ensuring that all records pertaining to the $2,715,243.14 outbound wire transfer were included, along with the email correspondence demonstrating the lookalike sender domain and the urgency language that bypassed the dual-approval control. The records were submitted to the requesting agency on September 18, 2023.

Following the submission of the subpoenaed records, Cortex Bank and Trust received a subsequent written request from the Federal Bureau of Investigation on September 20, 2023. This request sought further clarification regarding the specific individuals authorized to initiate wire transfers on behalf of Greystone Ventures Corp. and the internal procedures governing the dual-approval control process. The reviewing analyst prepared a detailed response outlining the authorized signers on the account and the standard protocol for overriding the dual-approval requirement, noting that the urgency language in the deceptive email had been cited as the justification for bypassing the control in this instance. The response also detailed the timeline of the transfer, highlighting its initiation just prior to the wire cutoff.

In parallel with the law enforcement inquiries, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a Section 314(b) information sharing request on September 12, 2023, with the financial institution that received the $2,715,243.14 wire transfer. The request sought information regarding the beneficiary account, including the identity of the account holder, the date the account was opened, and the disposition of the funds received from Greystone Ventures Corp. The request noted that the beneficiary name on the transfer did not match the invoicing vendor, a key red flag identified during the initial investigation.

The receiving institution responded to the Section 314(b) request on September 14, 2023. The response confirmed that the beneficiary account was held in the name of a different entity than the vendor invoiced by Greystone Ventures Corp. The responding institution also provided information regarding the flow of funds subsequent to the receipt of the wire transfer. The information received indicated that a portion of the funds had been rapidly dispersed to other accounts, some held at different institutions, while a remaining balance was still present in the beneficiary account.

Based on the information obtained through the Section 314(b) exchange, Cortex Bank and Trust requested that the receiving institution freeze the remaining funds in the beneficiary account. The receiving institution complied with the request, successfully freezing $597,353.49. The reviewing analyst documented the amount frozen and calculated the residual loss to the customer, which amounted to $2,117,889.65. This information was subsequently communicated to Greystone Ventures Corp. and incorporated into the ongoing investigation file.

The reviewing analyst maintained ongoing communication with the law enforcement agencies involved, providing updates as new information became available. The details of the Section 314(b) exchange, including the information regarding the beneficiary account and the successful freezing of a portion of the funds, were shared with the Federal Bureau of Investigation on September 20, 2023, supplementing the earlier response to their written request. The bank's records indicate that the law enforcement investigation into the matter remains active. The bank continues to monitor the account held by Greystone Ventures Corp. and will provide further information to law enforcement as appropriate or required by legal process. The coordination efforts have focused on providing a comprehensive factual record of the transaction and the circumstances surrounding it, facilitating the investigative efforts of the external agencies. All communications and disclosures have been conducted in accordance with established procedures for law enforcement interaction and information sharing under the USA PATRIOT Act.

## Filing Determination

Cortex Bank and Trust is filing this report because the activity described above is consistent with funds induced out of a customer account by deception and moved by wire to a beneficiary the customer never intended to pay and no legitimate business purpose was identified for it. The determination rests on the key finding recorded above. The relationship has been placed under enhanced monitoring, the monitoring scenarios that generated the underlying alerts have been retuned for this customer segment, and a relationship review has been scheduled. Supporting documentation is retained in internal case file FIU-2024-1737 and is available to law enforcement on request.

## Report Header

Filing institution: Cortex Bank and Trust
Internal case reference: FIU-2024-1738
Report filed: November 8, 2024
Suspected activity: sanctions / OFAC
Risk tier: low
Subjects of this report:
  Bluewater Freight LLC (business), account 79-39242-1
  Leocadia Abernathy (individual), account 12-93509-2
  Yusuf Jankowski (individual), account 68-81026-3
  Nadia Lindqvist (individual), account 53-94712-4
  Anvil Textiles Holdings Ltd. (business), account 23-78390-5
Review period: December 25, 2023 through November 8, 2024
Aggregate amount of activity reviewed: $3,752,788.82

## Activity Overview

This review was initiated following an escalation from the trade finance operations team regarding a documentary collection presented on behalf of Bluewater Freight LLC, holder of Cortex Bank and Trust account 79-39242-1. The escalation concerned potential exposure to a sanctioned jurisdiction that was identified during manual review of shipping documents presented on January 5, 2024, despite the transaction having initially cleared automated sanctions screening without generating an alert. The review period spans from December 25, 2023, through November 8, 2024, focusing on trade finance activity and associated funds transfers involving this customer. The activity under review involves an aggregate transaction value of $3,752,788.82, primarily consisting of international wire transfers and documentary collections. The suspected typology is the circumvention of sanctions controls, specifically through the use of transshipment hubs and potentially obfuscated counterparty details to facilitate trade involving a comprehensively sanctioned jurisdiction.

Bluewater Freight LLC maintains a commercial checking account at Cortex Bank and Trust, primarily utilized for processing international trade payments. The customer profile indicates the business operates as a freight forwarder and logistics coordinator. The activity prompting the initial escalation involved a documentary collection presented for payment on January 5, 2024. The operations team noted discrepancies within the presented shipping documents, specifically bills of lading and certificates of origin, which suggested the underlying goods were potentially sourced from or destined for a comprehensively sanctioned jurisdiction. While the automated sanctions screening system did not generate a match against the primary parties named in the payment instructions, the manual review of the underlying trade documentation revealed a counterparty address located in a sanctioned territory.

The initial escalation concerned a specific payment instruction associated with the documentary collection. This payment, valued at $880,898.39, was subsequently blocked by Cortex Bank and Trust pending further investigation and consultation with regulatory authorities. The declared value of the shipment named in the corresponding trade documents was $885,098.00. The discrepancy between the payment amount and the declared shipment value, while relatively minor, contributed to the overall concern regarding the transparency of the transaction. The trade documents also indicated that the shipment was routed through a known transshipment hub, a practice often utilized to obscure the ultimate origin or destination of goods, particularly in the context of sanctions evasion.

Following the escalation on January 5, 2024, a broader review of Bluewater Freight LLC's recent activity was undertaken. This review identified a second, distinct payment instruction that generated a potential name match during subsequent, enhanced screening procedures implemented following the initial incident. This second payment, valued at $510,130.38, was held pending resolution of the potential match against a sanctioned entity list. The review also examined prior transactions within the review period to determine if similar patterns of activity were present.

The analysis of the historical activity within the review period, which commenced on December 25, 2023, revealed a pattern of transactions involving several counterparties, including Hearthstone Metals Holdings Ltd., Harborview Produce Holdings Ltd., and Glenhaven Metals Holdings Ltd. While these entities did not immediately generate sanctions alerts, the nature of the transactions and their timing relative to the escalated activity warranted further scrutiny. The review noted that several payments processed in late December 2023 and early January 2024 exhibited characteristics that, in retrospect, aligned with the concerns raised by the January 5, 2024 escalation.

Specifically, the review identified instances where payment references appeared to have been stripped of detailed originator or beneficiary information, a tactic sometimes employed to bypass automated screening filters. This obfuscation of payment details, combined with the use of transshipment hubs noted in the trade documents, suggested a potential concerted effort to obscure the true nature of the transactions and the identities of the underlying parties involved. The aggregate value of the transactions reviewed, encompassing both the blocked and held payments as well as the historical activity, totaled $3,752,788.82.

The investigation also focused on the ownership structure of counterparties involved in the transactions. While no immediate OFAC matches were identified for the primary counterparties, the review noted complex ownership structures. In one instance, an intermediate owner of a related entity held exactly forty-nine percent ownership. This specific ownership percentage is frequently observed in structures designed to avoid triggering the fifty percent rule, whereby an entity is considered blocked if it is owned fifty percent or more by one or more blocked persons. The presence of this ownership structure, while not definitively establishing a sanctions violation, added a layer of complexity and risk to the overall customer profile.

The activity reviewed involved multiple individuals maintaining accounts at Cortex Bank and Trust, including Leocadia Abernathy, Yusuf Jankowski, and Nadia Lindqvist, as well as another commercial entity, Anvil Textiles Holdings Ltd. The relationships between these individuals and entities, and their respective roles within the transactions under review, formed a significant component of the investigation. The review sought to determine if these accounts were utilized in a coordinated manner to facilitate the suspected sanctions evasion typology. The analysis of these related accounts focused on identifying any direct linkages or shared transactional patterns with Bluewater Freight LLC.

The review of transactions occurring between December 27, 2023, and January 15, 2024, highlighted a concentration of activity involving the counterparties previously identified. This period included the initial transactions that cleared screening without issue, as well as the subsequent blocked and held payments. The timing of these transactions, clustering around the turn of the year, was analyzed in the context of the overall customer profile and the specific concerns raised by the trade finance operations team. The investigation sought to determine if the activity during this timeframe represented a deliberate attempt to exploit potential vulnerabilities in the bank's screening processes or if it was reflective of legitimate, albeit complex, trade finance operations. The focus remained on the discrepancies identified in the trade documentation, the use of transshipment hubs, and the potential obfuscation of counterparty details.

## Subject Background and Relationship History

Leocadia Abernathy established a personal banking relationship with Cortex Bank and Trust in early 2018. At onboarding, the customer opened checking account 12-93509-2 and a standard savings product, later adding a modest consumer credit line. The customer declared her occupation as an independent logistics consultant, indicating she provided specialized routing and customs clearance advice to small and mid-sized import-export firms. The expected activity profile documented at the inception of the relationship anticipated routine payroll deposits, consistent with self-employment income, alongside standard household and personal expenditures. The anticipated transaction volume was commensurate with the declared consulting income, and the account was assigned a low risk tier based on the domestic nature of the anticipated activity and the absence of high-risk indicators at the time of opening. Until the current review period, the account maintained this low risk rating, and the activity observed generally aligned with the expected profile of a domestic professional services consultant. No prior suspicious activity reports or unusual activity referrals are associated with this customer profile.

A review of the account history prior to the current review period confirms a pattern of regular incoming funds consistent with the declared occupation. These funds originated primarily from domestic businesses, predominantly limited liability companies and small corporations, bearing names suggestive of logistics, freight forwarding, or import-export operations. The outgoing activity was typical of personal expenses, including mortgage payments, utility bills, consumer retail purchases, and credit card settlements. The overall balance remained stable, and the transaction velocity did not exceed anticipated levels. The customer did not utilize the account for international wire transfers or foreign currency exchange services during the initial years of the relationship, further supporting the initial low risk assessment.

During the current review period, however, a significant deviation from the established activity profile was observed. The customer's transaction volume increased substantially, driven by large incoming wire transfers that appeared incongruous with the previously established pattern of consulting fees. The frequency and magnitude of these transfers exceeded the expectations set during onboarding. The reviewing analyst noted that the source of these funds shifted from domestic small businesses to corporate entities with complex holding structures, several of which are counterparties identified in the broader investigation. The activity no longer reflected the routine income and expenditure of an independent consultant but rather resembled the financial flows of a commercial enterprise operating in international trade.

The deviation became apparent when the account began receiving substantial, round-dollar wire transfers from entities such as Hearthstone Metals Holdings Ltd. and Harborview Produce Holdings Ltd. The transaction references accompanying these transfers often lacked detailed originator information, sometimes consisting only of alphanumeric codes or generic terms like 'consulting services.' This lack of transparency contrasts with the earlier, more detailed payment descriptions observed when the account was funded by smaller domestic clients. The receipt of these funds was frequently followed by rapid, large-scale outgoing transfers to other entities, a pattern inconsistent with personal wealth accumulation or typical household expenditure.

The reviewing analyst further observed that the customer's account served as a conduit for funds directed to other subjects and counterparties identified in this review. For example, incoming funds from Harborview Produce Holdings Ltd. were often followed shortly by outgoing transfers to Yusuf Jankowski or Nadia Lindqvist. This flow of funds suggests the account is being utilized to facilitate transactions between third parties, rather than serving its stated purpose as a personal deposit account. The customer's role appears to have evolved from a provider of consulting services to a financial intermediary or facilitator for a network of interconnected entities.

The customer's declared occupation as a logistics consultant may provide a plausible context for interactions with firms engaged in international trade. However, the volume of funds passing through the personal account, the use of complex corporate structures by the counterparties, and the rapid movement of funds to other individuals and entities indicate a level of involvement that extends beyond standard consulting services. The activity suggests the customer may be acting as a nominee or agent, utilizing the personal account to process commercial transactions and obscure the ultimate origin or destination of the funds. This assessment is supported by the observation that the transaction references were frequently stripped of originator detail, a practice that complicates the tracing of funds and limits the visibility of the underlying commercial activity.

The shift in account activity from domestic personal use to the facilitation of complex, high-value transfers involving corporate entities signifies a material change in the customer's risk profile. The use of a personal account for what appears to be commercial activity, particularly activity involving international trade and complex corporate structures, circumvents the bank's enhanced due diligence processes typically applied to commercial clients. The customer has not updated her profile with Cortex Bank and Trust to reflect this change in activity, nor has she provided documentation to substantiate the business purpose of the large-value transfers. The reviewing analyst determined that the current activity is not commensurate with the expected profile established at onboarding and warrants further scrutiny in the context of the broader investigation into the interconnected network of subjects and counterparties. The use of the account to receive and disburse funds on behalf of third parties, coupled with the lack of transparency regarding the source and purpose of the funds, presents a significant compliance risk and represents a departure from the anticipated use of the personal banking products provided by Cortex Bank and Trust.

## Account Profile and Baseline Activity - Yusuf Jankowski

Cortex Bank and Trust account 68-81026-3, held in the name of Yusuf Jankowski, was opened prior to the review period. The account was established as a personal checking account. The customer onboarding documentation indicated that the primary source of funds would be salary and wages from employment in the logistics sector, supplemented by occasional investment income. The anticipated monthly transaction volume, based on the customer profile and initial discussions with the relationship manager, was projected to be in the low five-figure range, consisting primarily of direct deposits, point-of-sale transactions, ATM withdrawals, and routine bill payments. The customer did not declare any anticipated international wire transfer activity or involvement in complex trade finance arrangements at the time of account opening.

A review of the historical account activity prior to the current review period confirmed that the transactional behavior generally aligned with the initial profile. The account maintained an average monthly balance consistent with a personal checking account used for typical household and living expenses. Monthly credit turnover typically consisted of regular, bi-weekly direct deposits originating from a domestic payroll processor. The aggregate value of these deposits formed a predictable baseline. Debit activity was characterized by routine expenditures, including grocery purchases, utility payments, and occasional domestic travel expenses, executed primarily through debit card transactions and automated clearing house transfers. The mix of transaction channels used was consistent with a standard consumer banking relationship, with minimal utilization of branch services and no history of cross-border wire transfers or complex financial instruments.

The statistical baseline maintained by the Cortex Bank and Trust transaction monitoring system for account 68-81026-3 reflected this established pattern of behavior. The system established parameters for expected transaction velocity, value, and channel utilization based on a rolling historical average. The expected monthly credit and debit volumes were established at levels commensurate with the declared income and routine expenditure patterns. The baseline did not anticipate any exposure to high-risk jurisdictions, complex corporate structures, or significant fluctuations in transaction volume. Prior to the review period, the account rarely triggered monitoring alerts, and those that were generated were typically false positives related to minor deviations in routine spending, which were quickly resolved during initial review.

The activity observed during the review period, which commenced on December 25, 2023, represented a significant departure from the established historical baseline. The reviewing analyst noted a substantial increase in both transaction volume and complexity, introducing risk factors not previously associated with the customer profile. The account, which had historically processed low five-figure monthly volumes, began exhibiting transaction patterns more consistent with commercial activity or involvement in complex international trade flows. This shift in behavior was particularly notable given the customer's stated occupation and the lack of any updated information regarding a change in employment or financial circumstances that would explain the increased activity.

The most prominent deviation from the baseline was the introduction of cross-border wire transfers involving counterparties and jurisdictions not previously observed in the account history. The transaction monitoring system recorded a series of incoming and outgoing wire transfers that significantly exceeded the established thresholds for expected value and velocity. These transactions involved counterparties with complex corporate structures, such as Hearthstone Metals Holdings Ltd. and Harborview Produce Holdings Ltd., which were inconsistent with the expected counterparties for a personal checking account. The nature of these transactions, which appeared to involve trade settlements or the movement of funds related to international commerce, was fundamentally incompatible with the established account profile.

The reviewing analyst quantified the extent of the deviation from the baseline by comparing the review period activity to the historical averages. The aggregate value of the screened transactions under review, totaling $3,752,788.82, represented an increase of several orders of magnitude over the expected transaction volume for the entire review period. This dramatic escalation in transactional activity occurred without any corresponding update to the customer profile or any communication indicating a change in the nature of the banking relationship. The velocity of these transactions, particularly the frequency of large-dollar wire transfers, further underscored the departure from the established behavioral patterns.

The introduction of complex counterparties and international wire transfers altered the risk profile of the account. The transaction monitoring system generated multiple alerts related to these new transaction types, highlighting the potential for exposure to jurisdictions or entities that required enhanced due diligence. The reviewing analyst noted that the transactions often involved intermediate routing or the use of correspondent banks in jurisdictions known as transshipment hubs or financial centers with elevated money laundering risks. This complexity was absent from the historical account activity, which was characterized by straightforward domestic transactions.

The shift in the mix of transaction channels also contributed to the deviation from the baseline. While debit card usage and automated clearing house transfers continued for routine expenses, the volume and value of wire transfers became the dominant feature of the account activity. This change in channel utilization, from primarily domestic, low-value retail transactions to complex, high-value international wire transfers, was a significant indicator of a fundamental change in the purpose and usage of the account. The customer did not provide any explanation for this shift, and the relationship manager had no record of any discussions regarding the customer's involvement in activities that would necessitate such transactions.

The analysis of the account profile and baseline activity indicated that the transactions conducted through account 68-81026-3 during the review period were anomalous and inconsistent with the historical behavior and stated purpose of the account. The significant escalation in transaction volume, the introduction of complex international wire transfers, and the involvement of unfamiliar corporate counterparties represented a material deviation from the established baseline. The magnitude of this deviation, quantified by the aggregate value of the screened transactions under review, suggested that the account was being utilized for purposes other than those initially declared, warranting further investigation into the nature of the transactions and the counterparties involved.

## Account Profile and Baseline Activity - Leocadia Abernathy

Leocadia Abernathy maintains personal account 12-93509-2 with Cortex Bank and Trust. The account was established several years prior to the review period and has historically operated within established parameters for a retail deposit account. The baseline activity profile established for this account, covering the twelve months prior to December 25, 2023, reflected consistent and predictable transactional behavior. The account maintained an average monthly balance in the low five figures. Monthly credit activity was characterized by regular payroll direct deposits from an unassociated third-party employer, supplemented by occasional, low-value peer-to-peer transfers. Debit activity was primarily domestic and consumer-oriented, consisting of routine point-of-sale transactions, automated clearing house payments for household utilities and credit card bills, and infrequent cash withdrawals at automated teller machines. The total monthly volume of credits and debits rarely exceeded a low five-figure sum, and the transaction velocity remained stable throughout the baseline period. No international wire transfers, whether incoming or outgoing, were recorded during the twelve months preceding the review period. The account was not linked to any business entities or commercial activity, and the customer profile indicated employment in a domestic, non-financial sector.

The monitoring system’s statistical baseline for account 12-93509-2 established thresholds based on this historical activity. Alerts were configured to trigger on significant deviations in transaction volume, velocity, or the introduction of new payment channels, particularly international funds transfers. Prior to the review period, the account generated no alerts for suspicious activity or sanctions screening matches. The established baseline indicated a low-risk customer profile with transactional behavior consistent with the stated purpose of the account and the customer’s employment profile. The account was subjected to standard ongoing monitoring protocols, with no enhanced due diligence measures deemed necessary based on the historical risk assessment.

During the review period, commencing December 25, 2023, the transactional behavior in account 12-93509-2 exhibited a marked departure from the established baseline. The volume and velocity of transactions increased significantly, and the account began processing international wire transfers, a channel previously unused by the customer. The aggregate value of the screened transactions under review during this period was $3,752,788.82. This figure represents a profound deviation from the historical activity, where total annual transaction volume was a fraction of this amount. The introduction of high-value international wire transfers fundamentally altered the risk profile of the account, shifting it from a low-risk domestic retail account to one facilitating complex, cross-border financial flows.

The deviation from the baseline was not solely quantitative. The nature of the counterparties involved in the review period activity also represented a significant shift. The historical baseline involved domestic consumer entities and an unassociated employer. During the review period, the account interacted with a network of business entities, including Hearthstone Metals Holdings Ltd., Harborview Produce Holdings Ltd., Glenhaven Metals Holdings Ltd., Ardent Textiles LLC, Tidewater Industrial Supply Trading Co., Obsidian Fabrication Holdings Ltd., and Harborview Textiles Holdings Ltd. The involvement of these commercial entities, many of which appear to be holding companies or trading firms, is inconsistent with the expected activity of a personal retail account and the customer’s stated occupation. The customer's profile contained no information to suggest involvement in international trade, commodities trading, or the management of holding companies.

The sudden influx of high-value international funds, coupled with the involvement of complex commercial entities, triggered multiple alerts within the monitoring system. The system identified the significant increase in transaction volume and the introduction of a new, higher-risk payment channel. The activity was flagged as inconsistent with the established statistical baseline and the customer's known profile. The reviewing analyst noted that the account appeared to be acting as a conduit for funds related to international commercial transactions, a purpose for which it was not established and for which the customer appeared to lack the necessary business background. The volume of funds processed during the review period far exceeded any reasonable expectation for personal income or standard consumer spending, further highlighting the departure from the historical baseline.

The analysis of the account profile and baseline activity for Leocadia Abernathy (account 12-93509-2) demonstrates a clear and substantial shift in transactional behavior during the review period. The established baseline of low-value, domestic, consumer-oriented activity was replaced by high-value, cross-border, commercial-oriented transactions. The aggregate value of the screened transactions under review, $3,752,788.82, provides a stark quantitative measure of this deviation. The introduction of international wire transfers and interactions with a complex network of commercial counterparties represent a qualitative shift that fundamentally altered the account's risk profile. The activity observed during the review period is not consistent with the historical baseline, the stated purpose of the account, or the customer's known profile, and it prompted the subsequent investigation into the specific transactions and counterparties involved.

## Customer Due Diligence File Review - Bluewater Freight LLC

A review of the customer due diligence file for Bluewater Freight LLC was conducted to evaluate the completeness and accuracy of the information retained by Cortex Bank and Trust. The review sought to determine whether the documentation on file was sufficient to support the stated business purpose and risk profile of the entity, and to identify any discrepancies or missing information that could impact the bank's understanding of the customer relationship. The file review indicated that the core identification documents for the business entity were present and current as of the last periodic review date. The file contained a certificate of formation and a certificate of good standing from the state of registration, both of which appeared valid. The business address provided matched the address utilized for account opening and ongoing correspondence.

The beneficial ownership certification on file for Bluewater Freight LLC was examined. The documentation identified Leocadia Abernathy, Yusuf Jankowski, and Nadia Lindqvist as the individuals with significant control and ownership interests in the entity. The file contained copies of government-issued identification for each of the named beneficial owners. The identification documents for Leocadia Abernathy and Nadia Lindqvist were current. The driver's license on file for Yusuf Jankowski had expired within the last ninety days; however, a note in the system indicated that a request for an updated copy had been initiated by the relationship manager during the most recent periodic review process. The ownership structure detailed in the certification indicated that Leocadia Abernathy held a controlling interest, while Yusuf Jankowski and Nadia Lindqvist held minority stakes. The documentation did not reveal any complex or nested ownership structures, and the stated ownership percentages aligned with the information provided during account opening.

The customer due diligence file was assessed for documentation supporting the stated source of funds and source of wealth for Bluewater Freight LLC. The initial account opening documentation indicated that the primary source of funds would be revenue generated from freight forwarding and logistics services, both domestically and internationally. The file contained a brief business plan outlining the intended scope of operations and target markets. However, the file lacked detailed financial statements or tax returns that would provide a comprehensive view of the entity's financial health and historical revenue streams. The source of wealth information for the beneficial owners was limited to self-reported statements regarding prior business experience and accumulated savings. The file did not contain independent verification of these statements, such as bank statements from other institutions or documentation of previous business ventures. The absence of robust financial documentation limits the ability to fully corroborate the volume and velocity of funds flowing through the account 79-39242-1.

The last periodic review of the Bluewater Freight LLC account was completed on January 15, 2024. The review documentation indicated that the account activity was generally consistent with the stated business purpose. The relationship manager noted that the customer had expanded its operations to include new international markets, which accounted for an increase in cross-border wire transfers. The periodic review included an updated assessment of the customer's risk profile, which remained at the low risk tier assigned at onboarding. The review process identified the expired identification for Yusuf Jankowski and generated a documentary exception. The file indicated that follow-up requests had been sent to the customer, but the updated documentation had not been received as of the date of this review. No other documentary exceptions were noted in the file.

The due diligence file included records of communication between the relationship manager and the beneficial owners of Bluewater Freight LLC. These records primarily consisted of routine inquiries regarding account services, wire transfer instructions, and requests for information related to specific transactions. The communication logs did not reveal any adverse or unusual interactions. A review of the transaction history in conjunction with the customer profile indicated that the entity frequently engaged in transactions with counterparties in the logistics and shipping sectors. The file contained copies of invoices and bills of lading provided by the customer to support certain wire transfers. The declared value of the shipment named in the trade documents for a recent transaction was $885,098.00. The documentation provided for this transaction appeared consistent with standard industry practices, although the file did not contain comprehensive shipping records for all international transfers.

The file review highlighted the presence of several related businesses and counterparties. The documentation indicated that Bluewater Freight LLC frequently transacted with entities such as Hearthstone Metals Holdings Ltd., Harborview Produce Holdings Ltd., and Glenhaven Metals Holdings Ltd. The file did not contain detailed due diligence information on these counterparties, as they were not customers of Cortex Bank and Trust. The relationship manager had noted in the periodic review that the customer's business model involved facilitating shipments for a diverse range of clients in various industries. The file also referenced transactions involving Ardent Textiles LLC, Tidewater Industrial Supply Trading Co., Obsidian Fabrication Holdings Ltd., and Harborview Textiles Holdings Ltd. The extent of the due diligence conducted on these counterparties by Bluewater Freight LLC was not evident from the file.

The review of the customer due diligence file identified an intermediate owner, Anvil Textiles Holdings Ltd., holding exactly forty-nine percent of a related entity involved in a specific transaction stream. The documentation surrounding this ownership structure was limited. The file contained a basic organizational chart provided by the customer, but it lacked detailed information regarding the beneficial ownership of Anvil Textiles Holdings Ltd. The presence of this intermediate owner, coupled with the lack of transparency regarding its ultimate control, presents a potential vulnerability in the bank's understanding of the full scope of the customer's business relationships. The file did not contain evidence that enhanced due diligence measures had been applied to ascertain the ownership and purpose of Anvil Textiles Holdings Ltd.

The customer due diligence file review also noted instances where payment references on wire transfers were stripped of originator detail. This practice, while not inherently indicative of illicit activity, limits the transparency of the transactions and complicates the ongoing monitoring process. The file did not contain any correspondence or inquiries from the relationship manager regarding this practice. The absence of clear originator information on certain transactions necessitates reliance on the customer's assertions regarding the source and purpose of the funds. The file review concluded that while the core identification documents for Bluewater Freight LLC were present, the documentation supporting the source of funds and the complex ownership structures of related entities was insufficient to fully mitigate the risks associated with the customer's international operations.

## Prior Alert and Disposition History - Leocadia Abernathy

A review of the alert history for Leocadia Abernathy on account 12-93509-2 indicated four prior alerts generated between December 25, 2023, and January 15, 2024. The alerts were generated by the automated transaction monitoring system and related to the processing of international wire transfers. The alerts were closed without further action by the reviewing analysts. The analyst rationale for the dispositions was documented in the alert management system. The current review evaluated those dispositions in the context of the recent activity involving Bluewater Freight LLC, Yusuf Jankowski, Nadia Lindqvist, and Anvil Textiles Holdings Ltd.

The first alert was generated on December 25, 2023, triggered by a scenario designed to identify wire transfers originating from or destined for high-risk jurisdictions. The alert was associated with a wire transfer originated by Leocadia Abernathy to Hearthstone Metals Holdings Ltd. The reviewing analyst noted that the address provided for Hearthstone Metals Holdings Ltd. was located in a comprehensively sanctioned jurisdiction. The analyst closed the alert on December 27, 2023, stating that the transaction appeared to be a routine business payment and that the customer relationship was established and well-documented. The analyst's rationale focused on the customer's history of similar transactions and did not address the presence of a sanctioned jurisdiction address.

In light of the current review, the disposition of the December 25, 2023 alert appears insufficient. ## Key Finding

The review established that Bluewater Freight LLC was operating as a financial intermediary for a sanctioned entity, directing funds through an account held at Cortex Bank and Trust. The determinative finding was the identification of a series of wire transfers, originating from Anvil Textiles Holdings Ltd., that were subsequently pooled and remitted to an external account. The reviewing analyst determined that on October 18, 2024, a consolidated transfer of $2,024,287.71 was executed from the Bluewater Freight LLC operating account to Crescent Textiles Group LLC, an entity identified on the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list. The payment instructions associated with this transfer exhibited stripped originator details, consistent with attempts to evade automated screening protocols. The funds were ultimately received into account 76-64981-9. This transaction, representing a significant portion of the aggregate value reviewed, confirmed the exposure to a sanctioned party and prompted the escalation of the case.

The responding institution confirmed that both Harborview Produce Holdings Ltd. and Glenhaven Metals Holdings Ltd. maintained accounts and engaged in significant wire transfer activity with entities located in high-risk jurisdictions. The information provided indicated that these transactions also lacked clear business purposes and involved complex corporate structures designed to obscure beneficial ownership. The information obtained through this additional Section 314(b) request was incorporated into the ongoing internal investigation and was subsequently provided to the Federal Bureau of Investigation as supplemental information to their initial request. The coordination with law enforcement and other financial institutions was instrumental in identifying the broader network of entities and individuals involved in the suspicious activity and in understanding the methods used to facilitate the transactions. The information sharing process facilitated a more comprehensive analysis of the risks associated with Yusuf Jankowski's account and the related entities, contributing to a more robust understanding of the potential sanctions evasion network.

## Filing Determination

Cortex Bank and Trust is filing this report because the activity described above is consistent with exposure to a sanctioned party or jurisdiction that screening either missed or flagged and the business escalated incorrectly and no legitimate business purpose was identified for it. The determination rests on the key finding recorded above. The relationship has been placed under enhanced monitoring, the monitoring scenarios that generated the underlying alerts have been retuned for this customer segment, and a relationship review has been scheduled. Supporting documentation is retained in internal case file FIU-2024-1738 and is available to law enforcement on request.
